page: Microsoft Azure E16-8s_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing a constrained core configuration. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The instance provisions 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, backed by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache. Vector processing extensions include AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside hardware-accelerated AES encryption. The instance does not include local ephemeral disk storage, relying instead on network-attached Azure Premium Storage, and contains no hardware accelerators or GPUs.

A key feature of the E16-8s_v4 is its high memory density, delivering 128.0 GB of system RAM, which provides an allocation of 16.0 GB per vCPU. Standardized benchmarks place its processing capabilities largely within the middle tiers: Geekbench single-core reaches 1208.0 and multi-core reaches 4696.0, while PassMark registers a CPU score of 8274.8 and a memory score of 2323.43. Memory bandwidth performs reliably at 40.84 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 29.3 GB/sec for writes. In application-focused metrics, Redis SET throughput achieves 6.84 million operations per second, and PassMark database operations score 2724.96. However, single-threaded throughput in stress-ng is in the lower quartile, and mid-sized language model inference is constrained by core counts.

The constrained vCPU allocation offers a distinct cost-efficiency advantage for database software that requires significant memory capacity but licenses software per compute core. By halving active vCPUs while retaining the full 128.0 GB memory footprint of a 16-vCPU host tier, organizations can curtail per-core licensing expenses. This balance makes the instance well-suited for relational database servers, in-memory key-value caching layers such as Redis, enterprise analytics backends, and memory-bound transactional applications that do not depend on high compute parallelization.

Configured as a constrained vCPU instance, it provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores and an expansive 128.0 GB of memory, yielding a 16.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The configuration features AVX-512 and VNNI instructions, includes no local storage, and contains no GPUs. Benchmark metrics demonstrate solid mid-range performance, with a PassMark CPU score of 8274.8, memory score of 2323.43, and Redis throughput of 6.84 million operations per second. While single-thread compute density sits in the lower percentiles, the high memory-to-core ratio allows organizations running licensed enterprise software to maximize memory allocations while minimizing per-core software costs. The E16-8s_v4 is particularly suited for in-memory caches, relational database systems, and data analytics pipelines that require substantial RAM buffers without requiring broad multi-core processing throughput.
